title: Intrinsic system clause of the triangle projection normal form
statement: Fix a finite field datum F, a prime l different from its characteristic, a finite extension E of Q_l, and finite-type F.k-schemes X,V,B,Y,D,Z [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the actual intrinsic unbounded semilinear system operations and realization [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections, lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting]. Let j:X→V, b:V→B and i:Y→D be open immersions, q:V→Y, p:B→D, s:D→Z proper, and b≫p=q≫i. For arbitrary system objects K on X and L on Z set M=J_j K, T=P_s L, K′=K⊗P_jP_qP_iT and C_(K′):S_sS_pJ_bJ_jK′→S_(ps)J_(jb)K′ the canonical proper/open compositor. Let gamma be the normalized proper/open mate and delta the normalized open tensor comparison [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization, def-exchange-projection]. Then, in traversal order, pi_s; S_s(delta_i); S_s J_i(pi_q;S_q(delta_j)); S_s(gamma_(J_jK′)); C_(K′) equals (S_s gamma_M⊗1_L);pi_s;S_s(pi_p);S_sS_p(delta_b;J_b(M⊗square.inv);J_b(delta_j));C_(K′). Here square:P_qP_iT≅P_bP_pT is the canonical pullback compositor. This is an equality of intrinsic system morphisms before evaluation or total limit, with no Cartesian, boundedness, Tor or constructibility hypothesis. It is the system clause only; no finite coefficient assertion is included.

proof.text: The finite-type schemes are Noetherian, so b and i are quasi-compact. Put M=J_jK and T=P_sL. Apply the intrinsic system clause properOpenProjectionMateSystems to M,T. This gives delta_i;J_i(pi_q);J_iS_q(a.hom);gamma_W′=(gamma_M⊗1_T);pi_p;S_p(delta_b), where a:W≅W′ is the tensor of the canonical square comparison.

Insert a.hom followed by a.inv, and use naturality of gamma at a.inv followed by delta_j. Apply S_s and postcompose with C_(K′). Apply first-variable naturality of the actual properProjection transformation for s at gamma_M and L. Expand map_comp and associate; the inverse square factor is exactly the one in systemRight. No arrow is evaluated and no projection or mate is inverted.
